reran: cmd.sh on w3-int, w3-base and the 2.13.18 jar: identical; HashMap and LinkedHashMap return Some(7) and are empty. 2.13.0 stores the value (HashMap(1 -> 7)); 2.13.1 loses it. Variants on w3-int and 2.13.18: when the function removes the key and returns None, mutable.Map(1 -> 1) ends with size -1; HashMap(1 -> 1, 17 -> 17).updateWith(1) leaves get(17) == Some(17) with size 0 and an empty toList; LinkedHashMap(1 -> 1, 2 -> 2) likewise. java.util.HashMap, LinkedHashMap and TreeMap.compute throw ConcurrentModificationException for the same function, and so does ju.HashMap.asScala.updateWith; TrieMap stores the value.
user_impact: A remapping function that also trims the same map, for example an LRU on LinkedHashMap that evicts the eldest entry inside updateWith: when the evicted entry is the key being updated, the caller gets Some(v) and the entry is gone (reproduced). mutable.Map(...) is a HashMap, so the default map is the affected one. Needs a side-effecting callback, which is unusual.
fixability: design question: support re-entrant modification (look the node up again after the call, or fall back to the generic get/update/remove path when the entry is no longer in the table; restores 2.13.0 behaviour at the cost of a second bucket walk), or reject it as java.util.HashMap.compute does (mutable.HashMap has no modification count, so detection needs one or a table/size comparison), and in either case say so in the Scaladoc. Behaviour-only.
regression: in 2.13.1 (scala/scala#8073, commit 0e726b7c7e, added the node-caching overrides; 2.13.0's generic implementation stored the value)
links: GC7/GA1: re-entrancy of another kind (lazy argument), separate cause. LM1 (#537): another mutable.HashMap fast path that disagrees with the generic one. KT1: updateWith/getOrElseUpdate on the Java wrappers. scala/bug#12069: an earlier defect in the same override.
note: Real rather than by design. The Scaladoc of mutable.Map.updateWith says only that Some(v) updates the mapping and that the result is the new value associated with the key; it does not forbid the function from touching the map, the generic implementation and six other map classes honour it, and 2.13.0 did too. Java's precedent is that such a function is a programming error (the compute documentation says the function should not modify the map) but that it is reported, not absorbed. The hunter understated the damage: beyond the lost update, the Some-to-None path unlinks through stale nodes and decrements the size again, giving a negative size and entries reachable by get but absent from iteration. No existing report found (scala/bug queries for updateWith return only #10949, #11004, #12069, #12586).
